texts.preamble: Varun Beverages Limited vs State Of Rajasthan Through Pp on 17 February, 2017 Author: Sabina Bench: Sabina In The High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan Bench At Jaipur S.B.Criminal Misccellaneous (Petition) No. 719 / 2017 Varun Beverages Limited Through Its Autorized Signatory Mr. Shiv Dutt Pandey S/o Sh. Lokmani Pandey, Having Its Registered Office At F-2/7, Okhla Industrial Area, Phase-I, New Delhi 110020 and Plant At Spl-1-159, Riico Industrial Area, Phase-III, Boranada, Jodhpur, 342007. Versus State of Rajasthan Through Food Inspector, Office of Joint Director Medical and Health Services, Ajmer Zone. __________________________________________ For Petitioner : Mr. Anuroop Singhi For State : Mr. R.R. Gurjar-P.P. __________________________________________ Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sabina Order 17/02/2017
texts.facts: Petitioner has filed this petition under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 seeking quashing of the Criminal Complaint No. 03/12 (earlier- 495/09), titled as State of Rajasthan Versus Ikramuddin & others, pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tonk, Rajasthan. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that two complaints were filed by the respondent against the petitioner on the same day. In the present case, the samples were drawn on 24.06.2004 by the complainant on inspection of the premises with regard (2 of 3) to 'Pepsi', whereas in the other Varun Beverages Limited vs State Of Rajasthan Through Pp on 17 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41840342/ 1 complaint, samples had been drawn on 24.06.2004 by the complainant from the premises in question with regard to '7 Up'. In the case relating to sample of '7 Up', petitioner had sought quashing of the criminal complaint 518/2009 registered under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 by filing S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No. 2756 of 2014. The said petition was allowed by this Court vide order dated 25.10.2016. Present case is covered by the decision given by this Court in S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No. 2756 of 2014 decided on 25.10.2016. Criminal Misc. Petition was allowed on the ground that cognizance of the offence could not be taken after expiry of three years from the date of drawing of the samples. Samples were drawn in both the complaints on the same day. Learned State Counsel has fairly conceded that the present case is covered by the decision given by this Court in S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No. 2756 of 2014 decided on 25.10.2016.
